scenario.title: Specific heat of a metal by calorimetry
scenario.narrative: A metal container of mass {mc:unit} contains {mw:unit} of water. A {mp}-kg piece of the same metal, initially at a temperature of {Tp:unit}, is dropped into the water. The container and the water initially have a temperature of {T0:unit} and the final temperature of the entire system is {Tf:unit}. Specific heat of water is {cw:unit}.

derived.name: Tf
derived.expr: round((mp * c * Tp + (mw * cw + mc * c) * T0) / (mp * c + mw * cw + mc * c), 1)

parts.answer: mw * cw * (Tf - T0) / (mp * (Tp - Tf) - mc * (Tf - T0))

scenario.narrative: A heat engine takes {n} mol of a diatomic ideal gas around the cycle shown in PV-diagram. Process 1 → 2 is at constant volume, process 2 → 3 is adiabatic, and process 3 → 1 is at a constant pressure of 1 atm. The value of γ for this gas is 1.4. {@fig}

vars.name: dT3
vars.label: offset of T₃ from the adiabat

parts.prompt: Find the net heat flow into the engine in one cycle. $T_1 = {T1:unit}$, $T_2 = {T2:unit}$ and $T_3 = {T3:unit}$. The universal gas constant is $R = {R:unit}$. 1 atm = 101325 Pa. {_0}{_u}
parts.answer: n * R / (gamma - 1) * (T2 - T1) + n * gamma * R / (gamma - 1) * (T1 - T3)
